data.bottom_line: Elevations above 7,000 feet have 1-3 feet of snow on the ground. Recent snow and wind are building drifts and slabs at upper elevations. You may encounter wind slabs above 7,500 feet on north- and east-facing terrain. If the snow feels stiff or slabby underfoot, then find a different aspect away from wind-drifted snow. Even a small slide through thin coverage could end a season before it even starts. Thin snow cover and unburied obstacles, such as rocks, logs, and stumps remain a significant hazard. We'll update the General Avalanche Information weekly until full-time forecasting operations begin.
